title: Arm Holdings (ARM): AI Chip Architecture, Data Center Disruption
body:
Royalty revenue is collected on every chip shipped using Arm technology. In Q2 FY2026, royalty revenue reached a record $620 million, up 21% year over year. As customers adopt higher-value architectures such as Armv9 and Compute Subsystems, average royalty rates per chip increase.

Arm’s technology is organized across three business units announced at CES 2026: Cloud and AI, Edge (mobile and IoT), and Physical AI, which focuses on automotive and robotics.

## Recent News & Key Developments [...] The RISC-V question: The open-source RISC-V architecture is gaining momentum in IoT and edge, with over 10 billion cores deployed. Qualcomm's late-2025 acquisition of RISC-V leader Ventana Micro Systems signals growing institutional interest. However, Arm's mature software ecosystem, developer community (22M+ developers), and performance leadership create significant switching costs. Arm's DreamBig acquisition directly counters RISC-V's modularity advantage by offering chiplet-based [...] RISC-V disruption: The open-source RISC-V architecture poses a long-term competitive threat, particularly in cost-sensitive markets like IoT and edge computing. China's push for semiconductor independence is accelerating RISC-V adoption. Qualcomm's acquisition of Ventana Micro Systems signals that RISC-V is attracting serious institutional investment. If Arm raises royalty rates too aggressively, it could accelerate customer migration.

title: China Blocks AI Deal (Manus): Cross-Border Investment Risk Expands
body: The transaction involved Manus, a Chinese-founded AI agent company that had undergone a complete offshore restructuring: the original Chinese entity was dissolved, the core team relocated to Singapore, and a new Cayman/Singapore holding structure was established. The company subsequently raised US-dollar venture funding and entered into an acquisition agreement with a major US technology company at a valuation of approximately $2 billion. [...] In April 2026, China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) blocked the acquisition of Manus, a Chinese-founded AI agent startup, by a major US technology company. This was the first publicly confirmed use of China’s foreign investment security review mechanism to unwind a cross-border AI transaction. The decision has significant implications for US venture capital funds, strategic acquirers, and institutional allocators with exposure to China-origin technology companies.

title: GV’s Dave Munichiello On Qualcomm’s Modular Purchase, The Firm's 10x Return And The Shift In AI Software
body:
The artificial intelligence space saw two major developments last week that highlight how technology companies are trying to manage the soaring costs and complexity of AI computing.

First, San Diego-based Qualcomm announced its acquisition of Modular, a Palo Alto, California-based software startup focused on making it easier for developers to run AI models across different types of computer chips. [...] At the same time, reports emerged that chip startup SambaNova is finalizing an $800 million funding round led by General Atlantic, valuing the company at $10 billion. Together, the two deals underscore a growing reality in tech: As hardware remains scarce and expensive, the software layers that connect these chips are becoming just as valuable as the silicon itself.

title: Oregon’s chip industry risks becoming ‘insignificant’ globally, state report says - oregonlive.com
body:
By 

 Mike Rogoway | The Oregonian/OregonLive

Oregon’s semiconductor industry is in decline and is “at risk of becoming an insignificant stakeholder” globally, according to a new analysis commissioned by the state.

The report by Business Oregon, the state’s economic development agency, concludes the Silicon Forest faces “long-term stagnation” because it is too reliant on Intel, lacks homegrown talent and faces regulatory uncertainty, high costs and a diminished supply of industrial land. [...] The report warns that big semiconductor companies are investing in other states that have more aggressive economic development programs and do a better job preparing students for careers in technology. It suggests Oregon seek to nurture new, smaller semiconductor businesses to reduce its dependence on Intel and other legacy chip companies.

title: Mahatma Mandir - Wikipedia
body:
Mahatma Mandir is a convention and exhibition centre located at sector 13 C in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India. It is inspired by the life and philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi. It is one of the biggest convention centres in India, spread over an area of 34 acres (14 ha; 0.053 sq mi). It was developed by the Government of Gujarat. Business summits like Vibrant Gujarat Global Investor Summit 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019 were organised here.

## History

[edit] [...] The convention centre has column free air conditioned halls with a capacity to accommodate over 15,000 people at a time. Its theatre style main hall has capacity for 6000 people. Exhibition halls are built over an area of 10,000 sq ft (930 m2). It has four seminar halls (three having seating capacity of 500 and one with capacity of 1000), seven high tech conference halls and a meeting room. The Mahatma Mandir Convention and Exhibition Centre by The Leela draws inspiration from the life and [...] from the life and philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi.
